name: Bain & Company
summary: Bain's consulting interviews usually start with a digital assessment and move to case interviews, which Bain says look at how you think and structure a problem as it unfolds rather than at a single right answer, alongside questions on your experience and why Bain. For other roles, Bain's careers site says interviews vary and may include a coding challenge, a portfolio walkthrough or a written assignment.
rounds: Application review, sometimes with a recruiter call
Digital assessment for many consulting roles: problem solving, communication and analytical skills
First round: case interviews plus questions on your experience
Final round: more case and behavioural interviews, often with senior team members
For non-consulting roles: a coding challenge, portfolio walkthrough or written assignment instead of a case (varies)
looks_for: True North: doing the right thing by clients, people and communities
Curiosity and a love of solving problems
Focus on results for clients, not just analysis

questions.text: Tell me about yourself and walk me through your CV.
covers: A short path through your studies and work, with the reason for each step
One or two results you're proud of
What brings you to Bain now

questions.text: Tell me about a time you were open about a mistake or problem when it would have been easier to stay quiet.
covers: What happened and why staying quiet was tempting
Who you told, how quickly, and what you proposed to fix it
How it turned out and what it did for trust

questions.text: Tell me about a time you helped a teammate succeed, even though it wasn't your job.
covers: What they were struggling with and why you stepped in
What you did and what it cost you in time
The result for them and the team

questions.text: Tell me about a time you chose a practical solution over a perfect one. Was it the right call?
covers: The perfect option and why it wasn't realistic
What you chose and how you made sure it was good enough
The result, and what you'd decide now

questions.text: Describe something you committed to and saw through despite setbacks.
covers: The goal and why it mattered to you
The setbacks and how you kept going
What you achieved in the end

questions.text: A private equity firm is thinking of buying a chain of dental clinics. What would you want to know before advising it?
covers: The market: demand, growth, competition and regulation
The chain itself: revenue per clinic, margins, dentists' retention, room to open more
How the investor could add value, the main risks, and a clear view on whether to proceed

questions.text: A sports shoe brand's profits fell while its sales stayed flat. How would you structure the problem?
covers: Flat sales but lower profit points to costs or mix: say so early
Checking price discounts, product mix, materials, shipping and marketing spend
The likely cause, how to confirm it, and what you'd recommend

questions.text: A food delivery company wants to launch in a new city. How would you decide whether it's worth it?
covers: Demand: population, restaurants, online ordering habits
Economics per order: fees, delivery costs, discounts, and when the city breaks even
Competition, a recommendation, and a way to test before a full launch

questions.text: Estimate how many hair salons there are in Bengaluru.
covers: Starting from population and how often people get a haircut
How many customers one salon serves in a day, with round numbers
A final number and a quick sense check

questions.text: Quick maths: if a product's price rises 10% and the volume sold falls 5%, what happens to revenue?
covers: Multiplying the changes: 1.10 times 0.95
The answer: revenue rises by about 4.5%
What it means: the price rise pays off if costs don't change much

questions.text: Your analysis points one way, but the client's chief executive strongly believes the opposite. How would you handle the next meeting?
covers: Rechecking your analysis and understanding the reasons behind their view
Presenting the evidence clearly and respectfully, and inviting their challenge
Agreeing a way forward, such as a test or more data, with the client team

questions.text: Why Bain, and what do you know about how it works with clients?
covers: Something specific about Bain's approach or people that matters to you
How it fits the way you like to work
What you'd bring to a case team

questions.text: Which industry or type of problem would you most like to work on, and why?
covers: A specific choice, not 'anything'
Why it interests you, shown by something you've studied or done
A question you'd want to answer for a client in that area

tips: Bain says there isn't necessarily one right answer in a case; it watches how you structure the problem and build on ideas as the case moves.
Don't force a memorised framework; adapt your structure to the problem this client faces and say why.
Practise mental maths: percentages, growth rates and break-even, without a calculator.
Practise cases out loud with a partner and reflect on the feedback after each one, rather than cramming at the end.
Bain's careers site says it never interviews over instant messaging and never asks candidates to pay; treat messages like that as a warning sign.
